Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: TunIXP active with 4 peers moderate participation

Confirms 'active with moderate participation'; code unchanged.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: This variable requires unique subscriber penetration, not mobile connections; the cited DataReportal figure (125-134%) reflects connections/SIMs, inflated by multi-SIM ownership. GSMA-based sources show unique subscriber penetration well below connection figures (historically ~58% in 2015; mobile-broadband-specific unique penetration 'just under 50%' in a later GSMA regulatory report); no current precise GSMA Intelligence unique-subscriber % for Tunisia could be verified via open search. Revised conservatively to the 55-69% bracket rather than guessing higher; flagged for human review to obtain a current GSMA Intelligence figure.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: Organic Act No. 2004-63 established the INPDP data protection authority, still in force. INPDP's own published legal texts state that Tunisia has NOT ratified Council of Europe Convention 108, and a GDPR-aligned modernisation bill was only drafted in 2025 and is not yet enacted — so the framework has not reached a 'mature, regionally-aligned' top tier. Score unchanged at 4.

Value Name: At least one Tier III facility
Comments: 2 colocation data centers in Tunis, Tier I-II small scale
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DataCenterDynamics (2026) confirms Orange Tunisia's newly inaugurated, independently reported Tier III facility near Sousse; ATLAX (Tunis) separately markets its own facility as 'Tier 3+' and Dataxion also operates a colocation site in Tunis. Taken together this indicates more than one Tier III-class facility, meeting the 'Multiple Tier III facilities' bracket rather than the outdated 'Tier I-II small scale' description (based on 2021 Cloudscene listings) in the original comment. Revised to 4, though ATLAX's own tier claim is a vendor self-description rather than independently audited.

This better supports the existing code; confirmed but evidentiary basis revised.
